assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based account of technological change, the race between education and technology, and the quantified labour-market effects of trade exposure together changed how economists and policymakers think about wage inequality, polarisation and adjustment costs. The work is empirically careful and has wide influence beyond labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Katz and Autor are central to the skill-biased and task-based framework. Autor and Hanson, with Dorn, are central to the China-shock evidence. Dorn is a major co-author, but three names are the maximum. The credit split between conceptual and empirical contributions is imperfect but defensible.
assessment.maturity: The core papers span roughly three decades, and the findings have been debated, replicated and refined. The long-run adjustment dynamics are a live research question, but the contribution is well established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the task framework or the trade-shock evidence as the primary discovery.
Dorn's exclusion from the three-name limit.
Debate over how persistent the trade-shock effects are, and how far the findings generalise outside the United States.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work built a formal, empirically testable political economics, covering electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal policy. It connects institutions to long-run development and policy outcomes, and it links to the economic history of the state, including fiscal capacity and the evolution of institutions.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini developed the integrated framework and the constitutional-design evidence. Besley, with Persson, developed the state-capacity analysis. The credit is concentrated in a small, identifiable group.
assessment.maturity: The work is more than 25 years old and has generated large empirical literatures. It has had time to be tested and extended, and it is not recent.
uncertainties: Overlap with the institutions-and-growth work already recognised in 2024, which may reduce the sense of novelty.
Whether the committee sees this as a single discovery or a research programme.
The causal identification behind some of the constitutional-effects evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade framework moved the field from country and industry level to firm-level selection. It explains exporter premia, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade, and it opened the way to a very large empirical firm-level literature.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central, widely recognised contribution. Helpman has a long record in monopolistic-competition trade theory and in firm-level extensions with others. Redding is influential in quantitative extensions but is a more distinct strand. Two names are the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of confirmation across many datasets and countries. The framework is now standard teaching.
uncertainties: Whether Krugman's 2008 prize reduces the marginal case for another trade-theory award.
Helpman's relative weight against Redding or other firm-trade contributors.
Sensitivity of welfare calculations to functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring intergenerational mobility at fine geographic scale from population administrative data changed the empirical understanding of opportunity, and it linked the findings to neighbourhood effects and policy. The approach of building large new datasets and combining them with credible causal designs is strongly aligned with modern empirical practice.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear lead. Friedman and Hendren are major collaborators on the mobility and neighbourhood-effects work. Katz is a substantial co-author on the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis but is better credited elsewhere on the list.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from about 2014 onwards, so the work is relatively recent. Follow-up and replication across countries are growing but not yet complete.
uncertainties: Whether the time since the main findings is enough for the committee.
Attribution among the large Opportunity Insights team.
Long-run durability of the neighbourhood-effect estimates and of cross-country comparisons.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structural methods for demand estimation in differentiated-product markets and for dynamic industry models gave economists and competition authorities a workable toolkit. They underpin merger analysis and measurement of market power across many industries.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (BLP) is the signature contribution on demand. Pakes also has an independent line of work on dynamic models (Ericson-Pakes) and on estimation. Bresnahan, Reiss and others made important earlier contributions, and the long credited list makes attribution contestable.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of use, with wide adoption in practice.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as primarily a methods prize and how it weighs the many credited contributors.
Sensitivity of results to modelling assumptions.
Competing claims from Bresnahan and the earlier IO literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, interest-rate rules and a microfounded account of monetary policy, is the dominant paradigm in central banks. Its influence on practical policy design is large and sustained.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread over eight listed names with different roles, including price-setting (Calvo), policy rules (Taylor), the canonical framework (Woodford, Gali) and medium-scale estimation (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets). Any three-name selection is partial and attribution is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and confirmation, including in the policy response to recent crises. The limits exposed by recent inflation episodes are a live debate.
uncertainties: Difficulty of choosing a defensible three-person subset.
Earlier macroeconomics prizes in related areas.
Performance of the framework in the recent inflation episode, which may affect how the committee views its standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The construction of long-run top-income and wealth series from tax records and national accounts reopened the empirical study of distribution. It produced new historical facts and new measures of offshore wealth, and shaped public and academic debate. Measurement is the core achievement, and I value it as a measurement contribution.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez built the long-run top-income series. Zucman is central to the offshore-wealth and distributional national accounts work. Saez also appears on another ballot entry, which suggests overlap in how his contributions might be credited.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the early 2000s, with extensions since. Data and method have been scrutinised, and revisions to some series are ongoing.
uncertainties: Disputes over data construction and the interpretation of wealth-concentration trends.
Policy and political controversy, which should not decide merit but may affect committee dynamics.
How much weight to give measurement against theoretical explanation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how a sender can shape beliefs by choosing information structures. They unify earlier communication and mechanism-design work and are used across theory and applications.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow wrote the founding Bayesian persuasion paper. Bergemann and Morris developed the information-design and robust-predictions programme. Selecting three names omits one of the four credited and leaves a partial attribution.
assessment.maturity: The foundational paper is from 2011, so the contribution is comparatively young. Its influence is growing, but empirical validation is limited.
uncertainties: Whether the time since the key results is enough.
The three-name limit versus four credited names.
Limited empirical confirmation compared with other candidates.
